voyage.content: Nice streets with lots of little shops and cafes to sit outside in the summer and watch people pass by.

voyage.name: Helmholtzplatz
voyage.content: Little park with cafes and restaurants surrounding it.

voyage.name: Kopfgeldjäger
voyage.content: Get your hair cut for €20.

voyage.name: Max Schmeling Halle
voyage.content: Named after the 1930s boxing great and home of the Berlin Füchse (originally from Reinickendorf) the premier Handball team of Berlin

voyage.name: Friedrich Ludwig Jahn Sportpark
voyage.content: A soccer and American Football stadium with track and field facilities which has been host to several important competitions in the past, including German Bowls (finals of the German American Football League) from 2012 to 2018.

voyage.name: Freibad Plötzensee
voyage.hours: May-Sep (opening period varies according to the weather): daily from 09:00
voyage.content: A public beach at the small natural lake Plötzensee.

voyage.name: Karstadt Hermannplatz
voyage.content: Built in 1929; large shopping center including clothing, book, and beauty products shops, a post office, and its own high-end supermarket, (probably only second to KaDeWe in the area). The grocery section of Karstadt has fresh meat, seafood, and cheese sections.

voyage.name: Marheineke Markthalle
voyage.content: A market hall with different vendors (mostly food and drinks) including butchers, bakeries, delicatessen, fruits and vegetables etc.

voyage.name: Markthalle Neun
voyage.content: A market hall.

voyage.name: Historischer Weichnatsmarkt Friedrichshain
voyage.content: An atmospheric Christmas market with a charming medieval theme.

voyage.name: Hardwax
voyage.content: The techno record shop in Berlin; huge back catalogue and weekly news from around the world; also reggae 7" and drum&bass.

voyage.name: Heisse Scheiben
voyage.content: Big second-hand record store.

voyage.name: SpaceHall
voyage.content: A large selection of electronic music, from the latest releases to older vinyl.

voyage.name: Flaming Squeegee
voyage.content: Funny, creative selection of rockabilly and punk t-shirts, bar, and band merchandise.

voyage.name: Nüx Siebdruckwaren
voyage.content: Friedrichshain is full of screenprinted t-shirt stores, but Nüx stands out with their high-quality natural-history-museum designs such as owls, fish, and foxes.

voyage.name: boxoffberlin
voyage.content: Only 100 m from Checkpoint Charlie you will find a small but very interesting place for extraordinary souvenirs and gifts made by local designers. The gallery shows changing exhibitions of contemporary art, films and more from Berlin artists and the little Café offers the best Espresso – fairly traded and organically grown, refreshing lemonades without artificial additives, »Berliner Weisse with a shot« ... in summer

voyage.name: Modulor
voyage.content: Berlin's biggest and best art, craft, and design supply store. A must-visit if you are at all artistically inclined.

voyage.name: Aufschnitt
voyage.content: Berlin's only 'textile butchery' sells pillows shaped like meat, made 'fresh' on the premises by Silvia – a unique and whimsical Berlin souvenir.

voyage.name: Schwesterherz / Küchenliebe
voyage.content: Two 'sister' stores next to each other – one is a well-curated papeterie, the other focuses on kitchenwares.

voyage.name: Mauerpark Flea Market
voyage.content: Great Sunday flea market for vintage clothing, furniture, rare vinyl; not many professionals. A typical Berlin experience.

voyage.name: Dense
voyage.content: Electronic music.

voyage.name: Der Plattenladen
voyage.content: Techno

voyage.name: Da Capo
voyage.content: Second-hand, rock, pop.

voyage.name: Hip-Hop-Records
voyage.content: Hip hop.

voyage.name: OYE Records
voyage.content: When this record store opened in 2002, it mainly specialized in Latin, Brazil and Italo house, disco and nu-jazz tunes. Today it offers vinyl from a wider range of genres including techno, electro and house.

voyage.name: Dodo Beach East
voyage.content: Punk, rock, reggae.

voyage.name: Mundo Azul
voyage.content: International children's and youth literature and music.

voyage.name: Jokers Restseller
voyage.content: For a wide variety of cheap secondhand books.

voyage.name: Tausche
voyage.content: Berlin fans from all over the world can be spotted with the television tower, the city map or Berlin’s area code +49 30 on their tausche bags with exchangeable flaps and insets.

voyage.name: Princigalli
voyage.content: Quality shoes and cosmetics for ladies.

voyage.name: Who Killed Bambi?
voyage.content: Colourful tops, bags & things.

voyage.name: Sgt. Peppers
voyage.content: 70s secondhand.

voyage.name: Pauls Boutique
voyage.content: Sneakers.

voyage.name: Eisdieler
voyage.content: Sneakers.

voyage.name: Hit-in.tv
voyage.content: Clothing store.

voyage.name: La Lampisterie
voyage.content: Great selection of old design lamps in a crazy shop.

voyage.name: Farmers Market
voyage.content: A small open-air farmers market right on Leopoldplatz.

voyage.name: Curry 36
voyage.content: Excellent pork sausage (German: Wurst) with curry ketchup and curry powder.

voyage.name: Hannibal
voyage.content: Serves burgers and weekend buffet breakfast, good cocktails in the evening.

voyage.name: Morgenland
voyage.content: Asian breakfast buffet on weekends (reservation essential!), restaurant and bar every day with good food for mid-range prices.

voyage.name: Mustafas Gemüse Kebap
voyage.price: Chicken döner with vegetable: €2.90, vegetable kebap: €3.50
voyage.content: Regarded as the best Döner Kebab in Berlin. Mustafas is a local institution and draws crowds of tourists and Berliners day and night. Expect to stand in line for 20-40 minutes to get your kebab, which attests to the reputation that this place has. Drink beer from the convenience store while you wait.

voyage.name: Nil
voyage.content: Sudanese fast food shop, serves excellent falafel and other Arabic snacks together with peanut sauce.

voyage.name: Sarod's Thai Restaurant
voyage.content: This authentic Thai restaurant offers great food made from fresh ingredients. The ambiente and staff are nice and friendly, and they know English (and Thai, for that matter). Most meals are available as a small portion.

voyage.name: Tiki Heart
voyage.content: Innovative and creative Asian, Polynesian and South American breakfast.

voyage.name: To Loc
voyage.content: Indochinese cuisine. Some consider it the best Asian kitchen in the neighborhood.

voyage.name: Hamy Cafe
voyage.content: Delicious Vietnamese cuisine, a main course for €4.90. They have a daily changing menu and great lassis.

voyage.name: Kantina von Hugo
voyage.content: Small cozy Mediterranean mama-style home cooking situated near the Landwehrkanal. The menu is small but changes everyday. Friendly and not too expensive, very nice wines. Fresh pasta is a must.

voyage.name: Angus Restaurant Steak-Haus
voyage.content: Pizza, pasta, different steaks etc. It's one of the cheapest restaurants in Kreuzberg and because of this very crowded (which is part of the nice atmosphere).

voyage.name: Asador Steakhouse
voyage.content: Spanish and Argentinian food. Food is good and portions are not so small, waiters are able to speak English. Have a look at the water and drink prices and the taxes to avoid surprises.

voyage.name: Café Sarotti-Höfe
voyage.content: In a former chocolate factory. Buffet for €12, brunch on Sunday for €14.90.

voyage.name: Hasir
voyage.price: Main courses still a steal at €6-11
voyage.content: The flagship of a chain run by Mehmet Aygun, who has a pretty good claim to inventing the döner kebab as we know it.

voyage.name: Kuchenkaiser
voyage.content: Institution for generation 68, breakfast till 16:00 and global kitchen highlights every week.

voyage.name: RosaCaleta
voyage.content: Jamaican-European fusion food.

voyage.name: Restaurant Tim Raue
voyage.content: Michelin-restaurant serving Asian fusion dishes.

voyage.name: Burgeramt
voyage.price: €7.50 for a basic burger, €4.50 for fries.
voyage.content: Huge selection of gourmet burgers at reasonable prices. Mediterranean, gorgonzola/walnut, vegetarian, etc., with plenty of homemade relishes and dressings. There is a take-away shop in no 22 and a restaurant in no 21, but the benches outside the take-away shop are crowded, especially in summer.

voyage.name: Nil Sudanesische Spezialitäten
voyage.content: Unique place with ethnic cuisine from Sudan. Wonderful place for anybody who would like to taste something from Africa, like quark cheese with fenugreek and black cumin or peanut soup - different and original.

voyage.name: Lagom
voyage.content: Restaurant and cocktail bar. Free wireless Internet

voyage.name: Fischschuppen
voyage.content: Very fresh and good fish. Select your fish and have the chef cook it.

voyage.name: Freischwimmer
voyage.content: Beautiful waterside restaurant on a wooden quay with European dishes and a relaxing view on the Flutgraben river branch.

voyage.name: Lisboa Bar am Boxi
voyage.content: Portuguese tapas, bread, wine, beer and coffee. Good place to have a real dinner or just hang our and share a bottle of wine with a couple of tapas

voyage.name: Mutzenbacher
voyage.content: Austrian restaurant. The best schnitzels in the area. The vegetables are great too.

voyage.name: Schneeweiss
voyage.content: Very white and clean but still cozy restaurant with knodels, schnitzel and other German food. Very popular, so make a reservation. Has a great Sunday brunch with a buffet of dishes in individual glass jars.

voyage.name: Schoenbrunn Restaurant
voyage.content: The Schoenbrunn Restaurant is in the Volkspark Friedrichshain next to "Großer Teich". There's also a beergarden where you can sit outside in the sun.

voyage.name: Turnhalle
voyage.content: This big old gym is turned into a spacious restaurant, lounge and cocktail bar. Free wireless internet.

voyage.name: Bangkok Treffpunkt
voyage.content: Thai restaurant. Excellent service. Recommended for value and food quality by many in the tourist scene. Has same prices as in 1996.

voyage.name: Butter
voyage.content: Good food, nice salads, reasonable prices.

voyage.name: Kleine Eiszeit
voyage.content: The best ice-cream in Prenzlauer Berg, expect a long queue, closed in winter.

voyage.name: Konnopke's Imbiß
voyage.content: Known for their Currywurst and their good curry sausage. A local would ask for a "Curry mit 'ner Schrippe" (a Currywurst with a roll). Since 1930.

voyage.name: Neugrüns Köche
voyage.content: Modern German kitchen with daily changing menus. Opens at 18:00.

voyage.name: Pizzeria I Due Forni
voyage.content: Water (Tafelwasser) is free, a rarity in Germany.

voyage.name: Prater
voyage.content: A beer garden with a restaurant under shady chestnut trees. The oldest beer garden in Berlin.

voyage.name: FrischeParadies Bistro
voyage.content: Small bistro inside upscale supermarket. Sit at the small tables or at the bar, where you can watch the chef prepare your meal from scratch with fresh high quality ingredients. The food is simple and fresh, always excellent cuts of meat or fish. The wine by the glass is a good deal, which you know because you can pick up a bottle from the wine-rack behind you when you leave.

voyage.name: Agni
voyage.content: Excellent Indian food.

voyage.name: Knodelwirtschaft NORD
voyage.content: Traditional German dumpling place. Food and service is great

voyage.name: St. Bess
voyage.content: A restaurant making very good pizza with vegetarian or vegan toppings. Their wood-fired oven is right at the entrance of the place, and you sit downstairs in the basement (or outside in summer).

voyage.name: Gaststätte Deichgraf
voyage.price: Mains €7-14 (you'll find enough options at both ends)
voyage.content: Good German food. Has a nice outside seating area in summer covered by trees.

voyage.name: Bar 11
voyage.content: Bar in the heart of Kreuzberg, DJs on the weekend (rock, pop, funk, soul, disco), entrance is free and international audience. Mondays all cocktails half price.

voyage.name: Bar Sofia
voyage.content: Small café and bar with a bit tacky but very nice interior. Open daily from 09:00. Hot drinks till 20:00, alcoholic drinks from 18:00. Outside sitting permitted only until 00:00.

voyage.name: Café Wendel
voyage.content: Cozy retro-style bar with a lot of vintage furnishings, graffiti and typographic artworks on the wall, a large selection of beverages including bio drinks and regularly live music.

voyage.name: Crack Bellmer
voyage.content: Popular bar-club, offering live music, funk, disco and house music in an old brick building on the RAW compound.

voyage.name: Die Legende von Paula und Ben
voyage.content: Small and cosy bar with a large choice of cocktails, spirits and wine. For those who are hungry this place serves tapas and for those who want to smoke some cigars.

voyage.name: Galander Haifischbar
voyage.content: Bar with sushi and excellent cocktail and whiskey selection.

voyage.name: Holzmarkt 25
voyage.content: Sort of a cultural village at the Spree River founded by an alternative cooperative with a restaurant, bar, club, beer garden, an acrobat's hall, music studios and a bakery.

voyage.name: Hops and Barley Hausbrauerei
voyage.content: Microbrewery in former butcher shop. They have a good selections on tap, all own production and from other microbreweries.

voyage.name: Madame CLAUDE
voyage.content: Gigs 5 days a week (indie-rock, experimental, folk). Crazy decor (everything is upside-down). Open daily from 18:00 till late.

voyage.name: Orient Lounge
voyage.content: Relaxing lounge with good drinks.

voyage.name: Wild at Heart
voyage.content: Punkrock Club with live music, great deco.

voyage.name: Wirtschaftswunder
voyage.content: Synonymous with the expression "economic miracle". The prices are very low and it has a good local Kreuzberg atmosphere.

voyage.name: Wuergeengel
voyage.content: Great bar for cocktails. Fills up fast even on weekdays and is very crowded on Fridays and Saturdays.

voyage.name: Zyankali Bar
voyage.content: The most adventurous bar in Berlin. You'll be surprised what kind of drinks they have on their beverage list. They say some people entered the Zyankali and never came out again.

voyage.name: Noble Rot
voyage.hours: Tue-Sat from 17:00, Sun from 14:00, closed Mon
voyage.content: Cozy wine bar with a selection of interesting German wines. And some Hungarian. They also serve delicious sausages and cheeses.

voyage.name: About Blank
voyage.content: This techno club founded by a leftist collective is in a rundown industrial area. The club is known for its endless niches and corners and has two floors and a garden. Guests should know which DJs are playing this night.

voyage.name: Astra Kulturhaus
voyage.content: Popular nightclub and concert venue on the RAW compound with beergarden and international bookings.

voyage.name: Badehaus
voyage.content: Nightclub on the RAW compound, offering indie and jazz concerts, hip hop jams and house music in an old industrial building.

voyage.name: Berghain/Panorama Bar
voyage.content: Techno club in an old cogeneration plant near the Ostbahnhof. It has a huge dancefloor and room for more than 1500 people. Panorama Bar upstairs is open late until Sunday afternoon. Gay friendly, with hidden darkrooms and leatherboys. Be prepared for tough door policy on popular nights. Not for teenagers, no cameras allowed (mobile phones with a camera are allowed, but holders are expressly warned not to use them).

voyage.name: Cassiopeia
voyage.content: Eclectic mix of shows on, most nights of the week. good hip hop, reggae, drum’n’bass and electro events across 3 rooms and a terrace in an old factory. €5-10 entry. Opens about 10 but typically quiet until 00:00-01:00. Good strip of small vegetarian cafes in the same alley if you need to kill some time. Beers €2.50.

voyage.name: Club der Visionäre
voyage.content: Atmospheric club at the waterside well-known for minimal techno, house and techno-house and high-grade DJ bookings. Originally only a summer venue, it now also has an indoor winter location at the MS Hoppetosse excursion ship which is docked nearby.

voyage.name: Gretchen
voyage.content: Drum ’n’ Bass, Latin, hip-hop and Afrobeat club within a vaulted former military horse stable.

voyage.name: Hoppetosse
voyage.content: This is a club for minimal techno and house located on a permanently docked excursion ship on the Spree river, the MS Hoppetosse. It is the winter venue for the Club der Visionäre. It has one dance floor and a Martion Bullfrog sound system.

voyage.name: IPSE
voyage.content: This techno club began as a cozy, wild and wooden open-air club at the waterside for the summer season, but now also offers two indoor dancefloors. It is behind the Freischwimme restaurant. The warehouse-like mainfloor has a decent Kirsch audio system.

voyage.name: K17
voyage.content: 4 floors of goth, industrial, synthpop, post-punk, wave, metal, hardcore and punk, in a backstreet of Friedrichshain. Impressive exterior and outdoor bar. Less snobby than some goth clubs, but the unofficial dress code is all black.

voyage.name: Kater Blau
voyage.content: Techno club at the Spree river with an open-air area. DJs from the in-house label Katermukke play here regularly.

voyage.name: Lokschuppen Berlin
voyage.content: Techno club with an indoor dancefloor in a former railway depot, an outdoor dancefloor and a garden. It is 100 meters away from the Warschauer Straße S-Bahn station on the former RAW railway compound. Techno, electro and house bookings.

voyage.name: L.U.X.
voyage.content: This club in a decommissioned industrial building pours on the charm with its old pipes and control panels. DJ are playing electro, funk, nu disco or salsa in this often artfully decorated venue. Inexpensive drinks and bio beer available.

voyage.name: Matrix
voyage.content: This long-standing dance music club is located within ten claybrick vaults beneath the Warschauer Straße U-Bahn station. Once purely electronic, it nowadays offers a wide range of dance music genres. With its sociable atmosphere it attracts a predominantly younger party crowd which is not fixed on a certain genre.

voyage.name: OST
voyage.content: This techno club in a former harbor generating plant is the successor of the noted Magdalena club and has a huge dance floor and an audio system designed by Gary Stewart.

voyage.name: Prince Charles
voyage.content: This is a house and hip-hop club in the facilities of a former indoor swimming pool. It is decorated with light bulbs hanging from the ceiling, a wooden DJ booth and dancefloor and the bar is in the dry swimming pool. It is known for high-grade house bookings and has a Funktion One sound system.

voyage.name: Ritter Butzke
voyage.content: This techno club on three levels with an old commercial building is known for its artful decoration. It has a dance floor called Dampfmaschine.

voyage.name: SO36
voyage.content: Nightclub whose roots are punk, nowadays plays different alternative and mainstream concerts. Don't miss the Gayhane, the Turkish "homoriental" gay party.

voyage.name: Wilde Renate
voyage.content: This techno club behind a wooden fence and with its numerous artfully decorated rooms is one of the most renowned in Berlin.

voyage.name: YAAM
voyage.content: Large reggae/dancehall, hip-hop and afrobeat club in the factory building which previously housed the clubs Maria am Ostbahnhof and Deli an der Schillingbrücke. A focus on street art and street sports and a beach bar in summer.

voyage.name: Al Hamra
voyage.content: Relaxed Mediterranean/Arabic style bar cafe serving good food, with occasional music and movies, has a separate smoking section.

voyage.name: An einem Sonntag im August
voyage.content: Iconic café-bar in a retro living room style right at the entrance of Kastanienalle from where locals overlook the neighborhood from behind large windows. With regular live DJs, readings and Hollywood swings on the street.

voyage.name: August Fengler
voyage.content: Longstanding and often crowded bar with kickers and small dance floor. DJs play indie, latin, disco or electro.

voyage.name: Café Hilde
voyage.content: A large bright corner cafe and bar. Direct fair trade coffee, organic teas & ice cream, home-made cakes. Evenings there is bistro food including pastas and salads.

voyage.name: Kakao
voyage.content: Popular cafe and bar specializing in chocolate, ran by the chocolate shop next door. Has a great view of Helmholtzplatz and good hot chocolate.

voyage.name: Kauf Dich Glücklich Café
voyage.content: This iconic café with its diversified collection of colored retro chairs and its wild, overgrown outdoor terrace which is so typical of the hipster-hedonist Kastanienallee-Oderbergerstraße heighborhood offers crêpes, waffles, housemade ice cream, and an excellent breakfast. On crowded weekends, count in some waiting time.

voyage.name: Kulturbrauerei
voyage.content: A former brewery which now houses many bars and restaurant. The Soda Club has an excellent bar.

voyage.name: Morgenrot
voyage.content: Alternative cafe serving vegetarian and vegan food, quite a recommended place for people interested in squats and related issues.

voyage.name: No Fire No Glory
voyage.content: Third wave coffee place with a beautiful terrace and homemade sweets & savory food. Its espresso blends include 'the coffee collective' Copenhagen and 'bonanza coffee heroes' Berlin. Pour-over coffee with single origins for a real caffeine high are obtained too.

voyage.name: Pfefferberg
voyage.content: This is a large former brewery compound which has been reused as a cultural and nightlife center with changing clubs, bars, theaters, restaurants, a large beer garden, a hostel and artist's studios for decades. It is a bit similar to the Kulturbrauerei but has been wilder and more run-down until its renovation.

voyage.name: Schwarz-Sauer
voyage.content: Very popular bar with a local and international student crowd.

voyage.name: Wohnzimmer
voyage.content: The first 'trendy' bar in this part of Prenzlberg and still very popular. Serves breakfasts and is open late. Separate smoking room

voyage.name: Zu Mir Oder Zu Dir
voyage.content: Retro-stlye bar with very relaxed atmosphere, genuine 1970s interior and excellent drinks. The prices are fair and the bartenders are nice. DJs play electro or soul.

voyage.name: Dunckerclub
voyage.content: Alternative, hard rock, indie.

voyage.name: frannz
voyage.content: A relaxed pop/rock club in Kulturbrauerei, also with live music.

voyage.name: Brauerei Eschenbräu
voyage.content: A small brewery. In summer, they also have a biergarden (one of the few in Berlin where you can actually bring your own food). Throughout the year you can drink their beer in the bar (no outside food allowed there). They also distill spirits (including whisky).

voyage.name: Vagabund Brauerei
voyage.content: A micro-brewery. You can drink their beer from tap (and other bottled beers) at their nice bar. Has some outside seating in summer. You can bring or order your own food and consume it in the bar.

voyage.name: BackpackerBerlin
voyage.content: Cosy hostel providing room types such as dorms and private accommodations. Bathrooms and rooms are very clean and you´ll be equipped with Wi-Fi, internet, free coffee/tea, washing machine, computers, common kitchen.

voyage.name: Hotel ibis Berlin Ostbahnhof
voyage.price: Double room €60 if booked in advance

voyage.name: All In Hostel Berlin
voyage.content: Silent back yard, built in 1911, factory loft.

voyage.name: A&O
voyage.price: Double rooms start at €24 per person, dorm starts at €10

voyage.name: Pegasus Hostel Berlin
voyage.content: 2-bed rooms start at €19 per person, dorm starts at €14. One of this independent hostel's main attractions is its large, green courtyard which hosts a beer garden, BBQ, table tennis and comfortable seating areas. They have free internet access, laundry service and multilingual staff. They offer accommodations from single rooms with showers and WC, to beds in dormitory rooms.

voyage.name: U Inn Berlin Hostel
voyage.content: Another cosy backpacker hostel that offers singles, doubles and dorms.

voyage.name: Sunflower Hostel
voyage.content: Dorms from €10/person, they also have doubles and apartments. The sunny side of Berlin, nicely decorated rooms.

voyage.name: Eastern & Western Comfort Hotelboat
voyage.content: Dorms from €16/person, they also have singles and doubles.

voyage.name: Baxpax Kreuzberg Hostel Berlin
voyage.content: Kreuzberg's first hostel (est. 2000) is just off the main drag. Facilities are well maintained with very clean bathrooms/showers. Young (twenties) and mixed crowd. Beer for sale at all hours!

voyage.name: Three Little Pigs Hostel
voyage.content: The hostel is in an old nunnery in Kreuzberg next to S Anhalter Bhf.

voyage.name: Grand Hostel Berlin
voyage.price: Rooms start at €17 (mixed 4-bed room) and go up to €40 for a private one-bed room
voyage.content: In one of Kreuzberg's "Kiez" a 15-min walk away from checkpoint Charlie. It's a renovated 19th-century building and all the interior is new. The service at the reception is also very nice and helpful.

voyage.name: Comebackpackers
voyage.content: They have a big common room, a full equipped kitchen and free Internet.

voyage.name: Die Fabrik
voyage.price: 2-bed rooms start at €49/room, dorm starts at €18
voyage.content: An old factory building turned into a hostel.

voyage.name: Riverside Lodge
voyage.content: Little hostel in the neighborhood of Kreuzberg.

voyage.name: City-Hotel Gotland
voyage.content: Bed and Breakfast. Staff speaks English.

voyage.name: Sarotti Höfe
voyage.content: 3-star hotel in a transformed chocolate company. Modernised rooms with good location to Bergmann Kietz. Known for its breakfast/brunch and good service. Popular with mid-aged city tourists in a small and cozy hotel.

voyage.name: Mövenpick Hotel Berlin
voyage.content: Uniquely designed hotel in Berlin's city centre, near Potsdamer Platz in the former Siemens building on Schöneberger Straße.

voyage.name: Alcatraz Backpacker Hostel
voyage.price: Double rooms start at €22 per person, dormitory starts at €13

voyage.name: Corner Hostel
voyage.price: 2-bed rooms start at €20 per person, dorm starts at €14

voyage.name: EastSeven Berlin Hostel
voyage.price: Dorm rooms starting at €13 in low season, €17 in high season
voyage.content: Private rooms also available.

voyage.name: Pension Absolut Berlin
voyage.content: Quiet location near Alexanderplatz. The guesthouse offers single, double, triple and fully served apartments.

voyage.name: Generator Hostel Berlin
voyage.price: 2-bed rooms start at €20 per person, dorm starts at €10

voyage.name: Lette'm Sleep
voyage.price: 2-bed rooms start at €24 per person, dorm starts at €15

voyage.name: Meininger Hotel Berlin Prenzlauer Berg
voyage.price: Double rooms start at €35 per person, dormitory starts at €19

voyage.name: Transit Loft
voyage.price: 2-bed rooms start at €71.50/room, dorm starts at €15 per person
voyage.content: Transit, Hagelberger Str. 53-54 (Kreuzberg) is also part of this hostel chain.

voyage.name: Pfefferbett
voyage.content: Central location, walking distance to Alexanderplatz and yet in another world. It's in an old brewery complex converted into a cultural center. Dorms, private rooms. Easy access also from Schönhauser Allee 176

voyage.name: Homestay accommodation
voyage.content: Reservations necessary, minimum stay two nights.

voyage.name: Hotel ackselhaus & blue home Berlin
voyage.content: In the centre of Berlin, 700 m away from the TV Tower, Alexanderplatz.

voyage.name: Red Rooster Bar and Hostel Odyssee
voyage.content: The Odyssee is independently run by a young crew - a real rock 'n 'roll place with a nice bar. This is a simple hostel which provides internet access, bicycle rental, and a bar (open until dawn).

voyage.name: Bed and Breakfast Ring
voyage.content: Bed and Breakfast. The staff speak English.

voyage.name: Frauenzimmer
voyage.content: Private accommodation for women, from women. Guestrooms and apartments.

voyage.name: Brandenburg Gate
voyage.content: The only surviving Berlin city gate and a potent symbol of the city. This is the point where Straße des 17. Juni becomes Unter den Linden. The gate was designed by Carl Gotthard Langhans in 1791 and was intended to resemble the Acropolis in Athens. The Brandenburg Gate now symbolizes reunification, after dividing East and West Berlin for decades. This is the site of Reagan's "Mr. Gorbachev open this gate, Mr. Gorbach

voyage.name: Pariser Platz
voyage.content: The large square in front of the Brandenburg Gate contains the French and American embassies, the rebuilt Hotel Adlon, and the new building of the Academy of Arts.

voyage.name: Russische Botschaft
voyage.content: A vast wedding cake of a building, built between 1949-1951 in the best Stalinist style and meant to symbolize the dominance of the Soviet Union in East German affairs before 1989.

voyage.name: KunstHalle
voyage.content: This former German Guggenheim branch is run entirely by Deutsche Bank since 2013. Compared to the Guggenheims in New York, Bilbao and Venice, it is a relatively small exhibition place. It usually hosts a temporary exhibition and is free on Monday, with a free guided tour starting at 16:00. Since the place is small and the name "Guggenheim" a very famous one, the place is often very crowded.

voyage.name: Neue Wache
voyage.content: Erected in 1818 to a classically-inspired design by Karl Friedrich Schinkel as a guardhouse for the imperial palace, since 1993 this compact building has housed a small, but extremely powerful war cenotaph, the Central Memorial of the Federal Republic of Germany, continuing its use under East German rule as the primary "Memorial to the Victims of Fascism and Militarism". The interior of the Doric column-fronted build

voyage.name: The Bebelplatz
voyage.content: Nazi Propaganda Minister Josef Goebbels made Bebelplatz (then called Opernplatz) infamous on 10 May 1933, when he used the square across from Humboldt University to burn 20,000 books by "immoral" authors of whom the Nazis did not approve. Their list included Thomas and Heinrich Mann, Arnold Zweig, Kurt Tucholsky and Sigmund Freud. Today a monument is the reminder, though it blames Nazi students for the episode. When

voyage.name: Deutsches Historisches Museum
voyage.content: German historical museum covering everything from pre-history up to the present day. One can spend many, many hours here! The building from 1695/1730 was the Zeughaus (Arsenal) until 1876.

voyage.name: Friedrichswerdersche Kirche
voyage.content: Nice church near Unter den Linden/Museum Island, finished in 1830 by Schinkel in English Neogothic style. Nice exhibition inside (neoclassical statues and an exhibition about Schinkel's life and work upstairs).

voyage.name: St.-Hedwigs-Kathedrale
voyage.content: A domed church at Bebelplatz/Unter den Linden, the oldest (mid-18th century) and one of the biggest Catholic churches in Berlin. Interior was redesigned in a modern style in the 1950s, but there are still many treasure chambers in the basement.

voyage.name: Tränenpalast
voyage.content: Millions of visitors leaving East Berlin by train said tearful goodbyes to their friends and relatives from the East at this former border checkpoint. Hardly a year after the wall came down, the building was turned into a nightclub until it was forced to close in 2006. It re-opened as a museum in September 2011 and now houses a permanent exhibition that brings the absurd normality of everyday life in the divided city

voyage.name: Gendarmenmarkt
voyage.content: The Gendarmenmarkt is a square in the Friedrichstadt with the Konzerthaus (concert hall) and in front of the statue of Germany's poet Friedrich Schiller, the Neue Kirche (New church) and the Französischer Dom (French cathedrals).

voyage.name: Neue Kirche
voyage.content: Berlin’s Deutscher Dom on the magnificent Gendarmenmarkt square is not to be confused with the Berliner Dom. It was built in 1708. Since 1992 a German Parliament exhibition can be seen here entitled “Paths, Loosing Track and Detours” or the development of parliamentary democracy in Germany – ways and roundabouts. No religious services are held here.

voyage.name: Französischer Dom
voyage.content: The French cathedral houses the Hugenottenmuseum. It represents the ongoing influence on Berlin by the Huguenots who emigrated from France after the revocation of the Edict of Nantes. Crown Prince Friedrich William encouraged them to settle here because most of them were skilled workers or otherwise useful to the kingdom. One memorable artwork, in room nine of the museum, pictures Crown Princess Dorothea exclaiming "

voyage.name: Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe
voyage.alt: Denkmal für die ermordeten Juden Europas
voyage.hours: Memorial open 24 hours, information centre Tue–Sun 10:00–19:00
voyage.content: A vast Holocaust memorial designed by the American architect Peter Eisenman. Opened in the spring of 2005, this gigantic abstract artwork covering an entire block near the Brandenburg Gate, including an underground information centre with extensive details on the Holocaust and the people who died during it. The blocks start out at ground level on the outer edges of the memorial, and then grow taller towards the middl

voyage.name: Museum für Kommunikation
voyage.content: The former Imperial General Post Office, now Museum for telecommunication and post with many interesting historical objects.

voyage.name: Memorial to Homosexuals Persecuted Under Nazism
voyage.address: Off Ebertstraße in the Tiergarten, across from the Memorial for the Murdered Jews of Europe
voyage.content: A cuboid made of concrete. On the front side of the cuboid is a window, through which visitors can see a short film of two kissing men. The video will be changed every two years and will also show kissing lesbians.

voyage.name: Pergamon Museum
voyage.price: Admission: €19, discounted: €9.50, children under age of 18 free
voyage.content: There are three huge collections housed within this grand building: the Collection of Classical Antiquities, the Museum of Near Eastern Antiquities and the Museum of Islamic Art. The Pergamon Museum was the last museum built on Museumsinsel (Museum Island) and was intended to house the great acquisitions brought to Germany by archaeologists of the eighteenth and nineteenth century. The museum's best-known attraction

voyage.name: Neues Museum
voyage.price: Admission: €12, discounted: €6, children under age of 18 free

voyage.name: Egyptian Museum and Papyrus Collection
voyage.content: Exhibits include the Egyptian and Prehistory and Early History collections. It houses the famous bust of Nefertiti (the legality of its acquisition is still contested by the Egyptian state which is trying to get it back, so you might want to hurry to see it there).

voyage.name: Museum für Vor- und Frühgeschichte
voyage.alt: Museum of Pre- and Early History
voyage.content: Museum for Pre- And Early History with objects from the Collection of Classical Antiquities in the Neues Museum.

voyage.name: Altes Museum
voyage.price: Admission: €10, discounted: €5, children under age of 18 free
voyage.content: The main floor houses the antiquities collection in an ongoing exhibit called "Neue Antike im Alten Museum" (New Antiquities in the Old Museum). Directly through the front door, entering from the Lustgarten (Pleasure Garden, now under reconstruction), there is a domed rotunda with red and white cameos, Greek-style, with statues of the gods. To reach the Hildesheim silver collection, go to the back of the rotunda, tur

voyage.name: Alte Nationalgalerie
voyage.price: Admission: €10, discounted: €5, children under age of 18 free
voyage.content: Specializes in 19th-century painting and sculpture; Monet, Manet, Cézanne, C. David Friedrich and other important 18th- and 19th-century artists are well-represented.

voyage.name: Bode-Museum
voyage.price: Admission: €10, discounted: €5, children under age of 18 free
voyage.content: The museum’s treasures include the sculpture collection with works of art from the middle ages to the 18th century. The Bode museum is best known for its Byzantine art collection and the coin cabinet.

voyage.name: Berliner Dom
voyage.content: The city's Protestant cathedral and the burial place of the Prussian kings. You can climb to the top and get a view of the city.

voyage.name: Stadtschloss – Humboldt Forum
voyage.content: Started in the 15th century and finished in the mid-18th century, the baroque palace was the residence of electors, kings and emperors until 1918, when it became a museum. The palace was badly damaged during World War II and later razed in 1950, replaced by the GDR with a modernist Palast der Republik. The Palast was in turn gradually dismantled at the turn of the century, as it was discovered to contain asbestos and

voyage.name: Fernsehturm
voyage.price: €13, children €8.50 (if prebooked, slightly more walk up). Discount with voucher from other attractions
voyage.content: At 368 metres, the Fernsehturm is Berlin's tallest and indeed EU's second-tallest building, complected between 1965 and 1969. The main function of the building is television broadcasting, but the shiny sphere atop the tower houses a viewing platform, a restaurant and a Berlin Tourist Information point. The viewing platform sits 203 metres above ground, affording views of as much as 42 km away and featuring a bar. Giv

voyage.name: Weltzeituhr
voyage.content: Built in 1969, this 16-ton, communist-era clock is one of Berlin's main meeting points. Each of its 24 sides corresponds to one of Earth's 24 time zones and it has the names of some of the world's most important cities written on it.

voyage.name: Neptunbrunnen
voyage.content: A bronze fountain by Reinhold Begas. It was erected in 1891 as a present from the city of Berlin to the Kaiser. Neptune, trident in hand, presides over the square supported by sea-nymphs with webbed feet carrying him on a seashell. Denizens of the deep (a seal, an alligator, snakes and turtles, among others) spray water at him in homage while languishing mermaids pour water into the fountain, clutching sea-nets overf

voyage.name: Rotes Rathaus
voyage.content: The town hall of Berlin is known as such because it is made of red brick, not due to its former political persuasion. There are nice Prussian rooms inside, which are worth a look.

voyage.name: Marienkirche
voyage.content: Gothic church, the second oldest (built in late 13th century) of the historical centre of Berlin. It's the highest church tower of Berlin (about 90 m), but seems rather small beneath the gigantic TV tower. The church tower was built in the late 18th century by Carl Gotthard Langhans, the architect of the Brandenburg Gate.

voyage.name: Nikolaikirche
voyage.content: Berlin's oldest church (1230) is a 3-nave hall church. It is in the centre of an area destroyed by bombs in the war which was then turned into a faux "old town" by the East German authorities called Nikolaiviertel. The area is more a hodge-podge of relocated buildings than an authentic reproduction, and the newly-built 1988 apartments that attempt to "harmonize" with the older buildings are embarrassing. The church i

voyage.name: Zille Museum
voyage.content: A museum in Nikolaiviertel dedicated to the Berliner artist Heinrich Zille.

voyage.name: Hanfmuseum
voyage.content: It is the only hemp museum in Germany; you can see the history of hemp, the culture and use of it. You can see hemp grow. There is a cafe downstairs, with an open WiFi access. Everything going on here is legal - including the hemp growing under artificial light (a low THC strain grown with a special permit) - but they do not refrain from political commentary on the legal situation of cannabis in their exhibits.

voyage.name: DDR Museum
voyage.content: A museum dedicated to everyday life in communist East Germany. The museum has very relaxed rules and you are allowed to touch and examine almost every object, which adds greatly to the experience.

voyage.name: Volkspark am Weinberg
voyage.content: This sloping public park is very popular among locals for sunbathing, relaxing, having a picnic or playing the guitar.

voyage.name: Park Inn
voyage.content: Small terrace on the top of the Park Inn, publicly accessible. Take the elevator to the 40th floor, and follow the signs up the stairs. Pay the attendant who also serves beer and coffee. Great views of the Fernsehturm. In the summer, consider base jumping off the roof with Jochen Schweizer. It is often closed in bad/windy weather, so look for a notice posted near the elevator that the terrace is closed.

voyage.name: Regierungsviertel/Spreebogen
voyage.content: The area to the north of Tiergarten, along the bow of the river Spree (Spreebogen), is home to the German federal institutions such as the parliament (Bundestag, in the historic Reichstag building) and the federal government, as well as the new central train station (Hauptbahnhof) across the river.

voyage.name: Reichstagsgebäude
voyage.content: This imposing building houses the Federal German Parliament or "Bundestag" and was completed in 1894 to meet the need of the newly-unified German Empire of the Kaisers for a larger parliamentary building. The Reichstag was intended to resemble a Renaissance palace, and its architect, Paul Wallot, dedicated the building to the German people. The massive inscription in front still reads: "Dem Deutschen Volke" - 'For th

voyage.name: Bundeskanzleramt
voyage.content: The building houses the personal offices of the Chancellor and the Chancellery staff. The Berlin Chancellery is one of the largest government headquarters buildings in the world. By comparison, the new Chancellery building is ten times the size of the White House. A semi official Chancellor's apartment is on the top floor of the building. The 200-m², two-room flat has thus far only been occupied by Gerhard Schröder c

voyage.name: Kongresshalle – Haus der Kulturen der Welt
voyage.alt: House of the Cultures of the World
voyage.content: Germany's national centre for contemporary non-European art. The house is a leading centre for the contemporary arts and a venue for projects breaking through artistic boundaries. This architectural landmark was an American contribution to the international building exhibition INTERBAU 1957 as an embodiment of the free exchange of ideas. Colloquially called Schwangere Auster (Pregnant Oyster).

voyage.name: Aquarium
voyage.content: The largest aquarium in Germany with over 9000 animals that are presented on three storeys in a historic building. Aquarium Berlin is found on the premises of the Zoo, but can also be visited separately. One of the best places on a rainy day with children.

voyage.name: Bauhaus-Archiv / Museum für Gestaltung
voyage.content: Closed for renovations; the temporary Bauhaus-Archiv is at Knesebeckstraße 1-2 in Charlottenburg. Building designed by Walter Gropius. Inside a museum, library, cafe and shop.

voyage.name: Bendlerblock
voyage.price: Admission and guided tours are free of charge
voyage.hours: Mon-Wed Fri O9:00-18:00, Thu 09:00-20:00, Sat Sun and holidays 10:00-18:00
voyage.content: The Bendlerblock building complex has long held ties to the German military, first serving as the offices of the Imperial German Navy and today housing the Berlin offices of the Ministry of Defense. It was here where, on 20 July 1944, Colonel Claus von Stauffenberg and other officers led a coup that sought to remove Hitler and the Nazis from power. They failed and were summarily executed in the courtyard, where a mem

voyage.name: Berlin Musical Instrument Museum
voyage.content: Museum established in 1888, with a collection of 3,500 instruments.

voyage.name: Siegessäule
voyage.hours: Apr-Oct: Mon-Fri 09:30-18:30; Nov-Mar: 10:00–17:00. 30 minutes longer on weekends. Closed on December 24
voyage.content: Want to feel like one of the angels in Wim Wenders' classic film Der Himmel über Berlin (a.k.a. Wings of Desire)? Climb to the top of Gold-Else, as the statue of Victory on the top of the Victory Column is known. Just don't jump off if you're not actually an angel. Unfortunately there is no elevator, so be prepared for 285 steps to the platform at 50.7 m.Else was built to commemorate Prussian military prowess in the

voyage.name: Schloss Bellevue
voyage.content: Official residence of the (largely ceremonial) President of Germany since 1994. Only Roman Herzog (president 1994-1999) actually lived here, his successors have preferred a quiet apartment on the outskirts of Berlin, but this is where the president will usually host guests and do public events. Guided tours are possible, but plan to book up to nine months ahead and be prepared for having to reschedule if the presiden

voyage.name: Soviet War Memorial
voyage.content: One of three war memorials in Berlin erected by the Soviet Union to commemorate its war dead, particularly the 80,000 soldiers of the Soviet Armed Forces who died during the Battle of Berlin in April and May 1945. Contrary to popular belief, it has not been granted extraterritoriality even though it was guarded by Soviet troops throughout Berlin partition despite being in the British, not the Soviet, sector. It is ho

voyage.name: Zoological Garden
voyage.price: €13, Zoo & Aquarium €20, students €10/€15, children 5-15 years €6.50/€10, family ticket: €35/€50, annual tickets available
voyage.content: The largest zoo in the world, both in terms of number of species (1500) and animal population (14,000). It is especially famous for its pandas. The Elephant Gate (Budapester Straße), one of the two entrances and next to the Aquarium, is a traditional photo stop for most visitors because of the architecture.

voyage.name: Hackesche Höfe
voyage.content: The complex consists of eight interconnected courtyards. Plenty of designer boutiques can be found here.

voyage.name: Neue Synagoge
voyage.content: Built 1859-1866 this is one of the most architecturally stunning synagogues in Germany to survive both the Nazi era and the war.

voyage.name: Old Jewish Cemetery
voyage.content: Considered the oldest Jewish cemetery in Berlin

voyage.name: Ramones Museum Berlin
voyage.alt: Temporarily closed, check website for updates
voyage.content: Pays tribute to the Punk band The Ramones. It displays more than 300 unique and original Ramones memorabilia. You can get a drink at cafe Mania inside the museum. DeeDee Ramone grew up in Berlin and the city is mentioned in several of their songs.

voyage.name: Kollhoff Tower
voyage.content: Includes the Panoramapunkt, the viewing terrace located 101 metres above ground, accessible by Europe's fastest elevator.

voyage.name: Sony Center
voyage.content: With an impressive, circus-tent-like roof over its courtyard and remains of the pre-war Hotel Esplanade incorporated into the modern structure.

voyage.name: Deutschlandmuseum
voyage.content: An immersive history museum, opened in 2023

voyage.name: Leipziger Platz
voyage.content: The octagonal square right east of Potsdamer Platz was recreated to resemble its pre-war layout, but the buildings are modern rather than historic replicas and much taller than their counterparts from before the war. There is a diverse mix of uses among the buildings, which include the Embassy of Canada.

voyage.name: Kulturforum
voyage.content: A collection of most important and architecturally impressive cultural institutions, including many museums and galleries, that was built in West Berlin next to the wall separating it from the Berlin historic centre, which remained in the East along with the original cultural institutions of Berlin.

voyage.name: Neue Staatsbibliothek - Haus Potsdamer Straße
voyage.alt: Berlin State Library - House Potsdamer Straße
voyage.content: Designed by Hans Scharoun.

voyage.name: Gemäldegalerie
voyage.content: The Gemäldegalerie contains an astounding array of paintings, including works by Rembrandt, Rubens, Botticelli, Raphael, Titian, Goya, Velasquez and Watteau. The collection contains works from the old Bodemuseum on Museumsinsel in the East, now closed, and the former Gemäldegalerie in Dahlem. Its strong points are German paintings of the 13-16th centuries, Netherlandish painting of the 15th and 16th centuries, Flemis

voyage.name: Kunstgewerbemuseum
voyage.content: The oldest museum of its kind in Germany which, despite great losses during the World War II, still possesses one of the world's primary collections of European applied art. There are two sections to the collection: one located at the Kulturforum in Tiergarten, the other at Köpenick Palace.

voyage.name: Kupferstichkabinettt
voyage.content: The largest collection of graphic art in Germany.

voyage.name: Neue Nationalgalerie
voyage.hours: Tue Wed 10:00–18:00, Thu 10:00–20:00 (from 16:00 free entrance), Fri–Sun 10:00–18:00, Mon sed
voyage.content: Spectacular building by Mies van der Rohe contains its own collection and temporary exhibitions.

voyage.name: Documentation Centre for Displacement, Expulsion, Reconciliation
voyage.price: Free (ticket needs to be booked in advance on website)
voyage.content: The Documentation Centre features exhibits, library and testimony archive about forced migration and expulsion of people in the 20th century. The main focus is on the fate of German refugees in the course of World War II, but that issue is presented in the context of the German attack on its neighbours in the war and the prior displacement and expulsion of other ethnic groups on the orders of the German government. T

voyage.name: Berlin Wall Memorial
voyage.hours: Memorial grounds daily 08:00–22:00. Visitor Centre and Documentation Centre: Tue–Sun 10:00–18:00, Mon closed
voyage.content: The memorial site stretches along the full 1.5-km length of Bernauer Straße. The listing marker points to the visitor centre. Various monuments can be found along the entire length of the street, documenting nearby escape attempts and tunnels; captions are in German and English. The documentation centre across the street on Bernauer Straße/Ackerstraße is excellent (although most of the documentation is in German). Th

voyage.name: Kapelle der Versöhnung
voyage.content: This chapel was built on the site of a church built in 1894 which sat on the "death strip" and was thus blown up by the GDR authorities in 1985. The chapel is the site of occasional memorial services for victims of the wall.

voyage.name: Museum für Naturkunde
voyage.content: More than 30 million objects in the scientific collection and a fascinating exhibition in one of the most significant institutions of its kind in the world. Some parts still under construction.

voyage.name: Art Center Berlin Friedrichstraße
voyage.content: Four floors of exhibitions with a relatively good variety of genres and artists. A very nice oasis of calm from the busy Friedrichstraße.

voyage.name: Galerie Eigen & Art
voyage.content: One of the most famous German art galleries, home to the Neue Leipziger Schule (Neo Rauch et al.)

voyage.name: loop—raum fur aktuelle kunst
voyage.content: Known for being the "incubator" of future famous Berlin artists. Primarily featuring sculpture video, and painting.

voyage.name: Berliner Ensemble
voyage.content: Contemporary theatre. The theater was founded by Bertolt Brecht after the war in what was then East Berlin.

voyage.name: Chamäleon Theater Berlin
voyage.content: Located in the stunning Hackesche Höfe in the Berlin-Mitte quarter, the Chamaeleon Theatre offers exciting cross genre variety and music shows.

voyage.name: Deutsches Theater
voyage.content: Classical theater with impressive line up of actors and directors. Some events have English subtitles.

voyage.name: Kabarett Theater Distel
voyage.content: Cabaret and comedy, political satire in German. Their home venue is in the Admiralspalast.

voyage.name: Kunsthaus ACUD
voyage.content: The ACUD arts centre houses a theater, a gallery, two cinemas, a club, a concert venue, a bar and several artist's studios.

voyage.name: Maxim Gorki Theater
voyage.content: The smallest municipal theatre in Berlin. It was an important venue for contemporary theatre in the German Democratic Republic (GDR). Nowadays its program continues with its political critique. Next to productions of classics, it has a big focus on new and contemporary writing and productions. It aims at being open to anyone regardless of their background. Sometimes plays the 3 Pennys Opera by Brecht.

voyage.name: Volksbühne am Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz
voyage.content: Sometimes controversial, modern theater.

voyage.name: Friedrichstadt-Palast
voyage.content: Berlin's biggest show with over 100 artists on the biggest theater stage in the world.

voyage.name: Komische Oper Berlin
voyage.content: Founded in 1947 and at the forefront of modern opera. Their orchestra also performs regular concerts. Guided tours behind the scenes are offered. Each seat has subtitles where you can choose your language.

voyage.name: Staatsoper Unter den Linden
voyage.content: The impressive building and royal history make the building alone worth a visit. The building reopened in December 2017 after extensive refurbishments and acoustic improvements. The general music director of the Staatsoper and its resident orchestra, Staatskapelle Berlin, is the conductor Daniel Barenboim.

voyage.name: Theater am Potsdamer Platz
voyage.content: Musicaltheater and Berlinale (Berlin International Film Festival).

voyage.name: Berliner Philharmonie
voyage.content: The Berliner Philharmonie is a concert hall with 2,440 seats in Berlin-Tiergarten (constructed from 1960 to 1963 and designed by Hans Scharoun) and the home of the Berlin Philharmonic Orchestra. It is a famous building with outstanding musicians. Reservations are recommended, but cheaper tickets are usually available 2–4 hours before the concert if not sold out. Every Tuesday (September to June) at 13:00–14:00, there

voyage.name: Hochschule für Musik Hanns Eisler (HfM)
voyage.content: The HfM offers many concerts by their students and other professional musicians. The concerts are held at various venues of the HfM, such as at Charlottenstr. 55, 10117 Berlin or at the address from this listing.

voyage.name: Babylon
voyage.price: Movies are around €7-9; some movies are free
voyage.content: Great cinema with a large program of non-mainstream movies. They have a working cinema organ, which is also played every Saturday for free midnight screenings of silent movies.

voyage.name: CineStar IMAX im Sony Center
voyage.content: The worldwide recognised theatre at Potsdamer Straße

voyage.name: CineStar Original
voyage.content: The "CineStar Original" cinema located inside the Sony Center at the Potsdamer-Platz shows only movies in original version (e.g. in English, without subtitles).

voyage.name: Filmtheater Hackesche Höfe
voyage.content: Very broad range of movies.

voyage.name: Kino Central
voyage.content: Repertory cinema located in an ex-squat.

voyage.name: Adlon Day Spa
voyage.content: One of the best spas in town, next to the Brandenburg Gate in the Adlon Hotel.

voyage.name: Club Olympus Spa & Fitness
voyage.content: At the Grand Hyatt Berlin Hotel.

voyage.name: Day Spa
voyage.content: In Riverside Hotel next to the Friedrichstadtpalast.

voyage.name: BlueMax Theater
voyage.content: Home of the Blue Man Group. Used to house an IMAX cinema.

voyage.name: Großer Tiergarten
voyage.content: Berlin's largest park. In the summer and on weekends you will see loads of families with their barbecues.

voyage.name: Legoland Discovery Centre
voyage.content: An educational attraction for children, featuring a LEGO replica of Berlin

voyage.name: Alexa Centre
voyage.content: A large shopping centre complex right off Alexanderplatz.

voyage.name: Galeries Lafayette
voyage.content: The German dependance of the Paris-based French department store chain is a testament to Berlin's newfound role as a fashion hub, and with its unique modern architecture, a landmark of its own. It is all about fashion - the best labels and the latest trends.

voyage.name: LP12 - Mall Of Berlin
voyage.content: The newest and the largest mall in Berlin with the well known fashion brands and a decent food court.

voyage.name: Potsdamer Platz Arkaden
voyage.content: A medium sized shopping mall with the usual variety of department stores and boutiques.

voyage.name: Quartier 206
voyage.content: Next door to Galeries Lafayette is this upscale department store focusing on high-end fashion, with some cosmetics and personal care products to boot.

voyage.name: ausberlin
voyage.content: Alternative souvenirs (design, fashion and small stuff from Berlin designers and artists).

voyage.name: Rausch – Chocolatiers am Gendarmenmarkt
voyage.content: The world's largest chocolaterie.

voyage.name: Kulturkaufhaus Dussmann
voyage.content: The greatest books and musicshop in Berlin with English Bookshop

voyage.name: Leila M
voyage.content: A large selection of music on CD & vinyl: romantic songwriters, inspiring pop-music, minimal techno, contemporary electronica and so on.

voyage.name: Rotation
voyage.content: Weinbergsweg 3 (Mitte). Offers a vast range of techno, house and electronica. Weekly news. Open M-Sa 12:00-20:00.

voyage.name: Witty's Currywurst
voyage.content: Organic currywurst and fries.

voyage.name: Mishba
voyage.content: Burritos

voyage.name: Johnny's Bar - Karibisches Restaurant
voyage.content: Caribbean

voyage.name: Curry at the Wall Berlin Mitte
voyage.content: A Snack Bar

voyage.name: Weilands
voyage.content: Salads, soups and other healthy food next to the Casino at Potsdamer Platz. Big outdoor terrace in summer.

voyage.name: Bombay
voyage.content: Excellent Indian restaurant

voyage.name: Die Berliner Republik
voyage.content: German restaurant

voyage.name: Ishin Japanese Deli
voyage.hours: Mon-Sat 11:00-21:30, closed on Sundays and public holidays
voyage.content: The restaurant has the atmosphere of a busy waiting hall, but the facts that it is often crowded, that there are many Japanese customers and that they are the caterer of the Japanese Embassy speak for themselves. Sushi, salads, Don, and Cey-Ro. Free green tea. Happy hour W Sa all day until 16:00. They also have a branch near Checkpoint Charlie at Charlottenstraße.

voyage.name: Midtown Grill
voyage.content: Following the tradition of the old American steakhouses, at Midtown Grill you will find the best steaks in town.

voyage.name: Ständige Vertretung
voyage.content: Ständige Vertretung stands for Permanent Mission. In times of the cold war the West-German Federal Republic and the East German Democratic Republic didn’t have regular embassies, but Permanent Missions in Bonn and East-Berlin. Nowadays Ständige Vertretung represents Rhenish food specialities and beer. Excellent tarte flambee (Flammekuchen).

voyage.name: ALvis Restaurant
voyage.content: ALvis Restaurant offers culinarian highlights made out of regional products.

voyage.name: Brasserie Desbrosses
voyage.content: The liaison of old and new in the ambiance of an authentic French Brasserie works perfectly with the Brasserie Desbrosses. Here guests may enjoy French cuisine in a carefully restored and leger ambiance.

voyage.name: Brasserie Ganymed
voyage.content: Good French cuisine direct at the terrace of the river and close to the theaters.

voyage.name: Brecht Keller
voyage.content: Famous basement restaurant in former house of Brecht with Austrian inspired kitchen (receipts from Helene Weigel), reservations essential!

voyage.name: Chi Sing Restaurant
voyage.content: Reservation are welcome!

voyage.name: Grill Royal
voyage.content: Best grill restaurant in town with divine steaks and fresh oysters. Reservation for every night is essential.

voyage.name: Ma
voyage.content: One Michelin star and 18 points from Gault Millau make this Asian inspired restaurant one of the best in Berlin.

voyage.name: Chay Viet
voyage.price: mains from €6.90, lunch offer €5.90 incl. dessert
voyage.content: Vegetarian Vietnamese family restaurant, many dishes are Vegan.

voyage.name: Cô Cô bánh mì deli
voyage.content: Baguette, the Vietnamese style. Fresh and very tasty.

voyage.name: Dada Falafel
voyage.content: Tasty falafel and other mideastern food. Prepare for long queues.

voyage.name: Lucky Star
voyage.content: As authentic as you can get in Berlin Chinese food wise. They also have "all you can eat hot pot" deal for €12.80/person (minimum 2 people, 2015), which even though it lacks some ingredients you would normally get in a hot pot in Beijing (more variety of mushrooms - here you just get champignons - tofu skin, etc), still tastes as it should taste. For the hot pot you can choose between clear pot, spicy pot, or split p

voyage.name: Amrit
voyage.content: Indian restaurant.

voyage.name: Kopps
voyage.content: Vegan restaurant with upmarket touch that specialises in rather typical German dishes like Roulade or Cordon Bleu that Vegans would normally not eat. Weekend brunch from 09:30 - 16:00.

voyage.name: Papa Pane di Sorrento
voyage.content: Italian family restaurant where supposedly stars like Brad Pitt and Katie Holmes have been sighted. It has the decor of a waiting hall and is often crowded and slightly hectic, but the pizzas and the tiramisu are still worth it.

voyage.name: Susuru
voyage.content: Stylish Japanese restaurant that specialises in udon dishes - Japanese noodles in a tasty soup. Be prepared to get a bit slurpy with your soup - it adds to the flavour!

voyage.name: Vedis
voyage.content: Vegan Indian restaurant.

voyage.name: Kuchi
voyage.content: Excellent sushi restaurant with a nice garden right in the centre of Mitte.

voyage.name: Imbiss Unter den Linden
voyage.content: It's a snack bar

voyage.name: Little Green Rabbit
voyage.content: Tasty Soups and salads in a quiet side street of Gendarmenmarkt, mostly frequented by the office workers around. They don't accept cash.

voyage.name: Good Time
voyage.price: from €15, lunch offers from €12 including a starter
voyage.content: Asian fusion food in a tasteful decor, also suitable for a business lunch.

voyage.name: Aigner
voyage.content: Haute cuisine mixed with influences from Berlin and Vienna (reservations essential).

voyage.name: Borchardt
voyage.content: Where the rich and famous go since 1895 - reservations and decent clothing recommended. Fin de siècle decor, attentive service. Famous for their Schnitzel. Their lunch offers start at €13.

voyage.name: Fischers Fritz
voyage.content: Offers a Japanese breakfast in the Regent hotel.

voyage.name: Lutter & Wegner
voyage.content: Berlin cuisine in top style, since 1811. They offer their own sparkling, red and white wine selections.

voyage.name: The Greens - Coffee & Plants
voyage.content: Stylish café located in an old warehouse filled with plants, most of them for sale.

voyage.name: Zur letzten Instanz
voyage.content: Often claimed to be Berlin's oldest restaurant. While there has been an establishment at the site since 1621, the current name dates back to 1924. What's more is that much of the original building was damaged in World War II and reconstructed in 1963 by the East German authorities to make it more "appealing to tourists". Still, Zur letzten Instanz serves excellent, albeit a bit price, German cuisine. In the backyard,

voyage.name: Barcomi's Deli
voyage.content: A deli with superb American cakes and cookies run by the American Cynthia Barcomi. Apple walnut caramel cake, Devil's Food cake, Lemon Meringue Pie, Triple Chocolate Cookies, they have it all. There are also bagels, salads and lasagna on the menu for the non sweet-tooths. You can try to repeat the wonder at home with her four recipe books. They also roast their own coffee which is excellent as well. Not so easy to fi

voyage.name: The Barn
voyage.content: A small cafe that takes coffee very seriously. Or, to say it in their words: "Please be aware that we have certain preferences when serving a coffee the way we believe it tastes best." Children are not really welcome, there is only a restricted area for laptops. Good sandwiches.

voyage.name: Café am Neuen See
voyage.price: Beers are between €4-5, giant pizzas are €8-9
voyage.content: A must-do during the day if the weather is nice. This cafe is more like an outdoor beergarden. Even though it's right in the middle of West Berlin, the "Café am Neuen See" is located in the middle of the Tiergarten next to a small lake. If you are a (romantic) couple, make sure to rent one of the rowboats and enjoy the silent and romantic scenery. The nicer the weather, the more packed this place gets. Don't even dre

voyage.name: Café Fleury
voyage.content: Cute little French cafe near Weinbergspark. Excellent breakfast and tasty baguettes. Tends to be very crowded on weekends, be there when it opens if you want to have breakfast. If it is full, try the small sister Petit Fleury on the opposite side of the road.

voyage.name: Cafe Solvey
voyage.content: Lovely little vintage cafe. While drinks and cakes are decent, but not extraordinary for Mitte, the decor is really cute and it is very quiet. A good place to relax and read a magazine or book.

voyage.name: Dachgartenrestaurant Käfer
voyage.content: Breakfast from 09:00-10:30 at the top of the Germany's parliament. You have to contact them in advance and need to show your ID, since the entrance is through the parliament building.

voyage.name: Ebe Ano
voyage.content: Nigerian soul food

voyage.name: Kauf Dich Glücklich
voyage.content: The café with its iconic colored chairs on the terrace which at the same time is a shop for fashion and design. The venue which is so typical of the hipster-hedonist Kastanienallee neighborhood offers coffee, crêpes, waffles and housemade ice cream.

voyage.name: Sankt Oberholz
voyage.content: A very Mitte place directly at Rosenthaler Platz where the new digital boheme is at home and supposedly new business ideas and startups are developed. Almost everybody has a laptop, conversations are rare. Goes by the nicknames "hipster hell" or "unofficial Apple store". They also offer coworking spaces.

voyage.name: Strandbad Mitte
voyage.content: Good breakfast and playground next to the restaurant.

voyage.name: Telecafé
voyage.content: Enjoy breakfast in front of a city view right at the top of the Fernsehturm.

voyage.name: Zimt und Zucker
voyage.content: A small and lively cafe in the style of the 20s. There is a terrace on the river in summer. Their German cheesecake (with Quark and therefore lighter than the American version) comes especially recommended.

voyage.name: Belushi's
voyage.price: Relatively low prices on food and drink
voyage.content: A popular English-speaking Europe-wide chain bar with one of the largest range of live sports events. A very relaxed atmosphere with a 5-hour happy hour each night. Belongs to the large Beds and Bars company.

voyage.name: FC Magnet Bar
voyage.content: This retro-style bar with its orange waiting room seats is a popular and often crowded venue for watching all important football games on multiple large projection screens, for dancing and for playing kicker.

voyage.name: Kumpelnest 3000
voyage.content: This tiny dive bar was founded in 1987 by an arts student and originally a venue where gay-lesbian, punk and postpunk guest mingled. While located in an otherwise emptied residential area with no further nightlife, alone the visual overexposure by its crazy decoration makes it worth a visit.

voyage.name: Newton Bar
voyage.content: Impressive bar that is the must hang-out place for the beautiful, the famous and the rich. Excellent cigar and whiskey selection.

voyage.name: Reingold
voyage.content: Lounge in a former locomotive construction hall (1930s style), mix of after work crowd and normal scene.

voyage.name: Riva
voyage.content: This stylish bar, named after Italian football star Luigi Riva, boasts a colorfully displayed curved ceiling painted in red, yellow, and purple squares. It's the perfect spot for grabbing one of the assortment of exotic martinis or champagne cocktails.

voyage.name: Victoria Bar
voyage.content: Comfortable bar with a huge variety of cocktails.

voyage.name: Weinerei Forum
voyage.content: This long-standing bohemian, retro-style venue offers vegetarian food by day and becomes a wine bar in the evening.

voyage.name: Cafe Moskau
voyage.content: Every Sunday night there is the GMF, a mainly gay party.

voyage.name: Club der polnischen Versager
voyage.content: From Polish films to country music, everything to make our neighbours feel like home.

voyage.name: Golden Gate
voyage.content: Dirty and dark after hours techno club near to Jannowitzbrücke with two floors.

voyage.name: Weekend Club
voyage.content: The Weekend is a rooftop club on the historic Haus des Reisens high-rise building with a view over the Alexanderplatz and the Fernsehturm. The rooftop garden is on the 17th floor. The music played is hip hop, R'n'B, Afrobeats and Latin music.

voyage.name: KitKatClub
voyage.content: The clubbing concept of the KitKatClub is mixing techno/electro/trance music with fetish parties. Nonstop party from Saturday night to Sunday evening. Be careful and open-minded, and respect the strict dresscode of fetish, latex, leather, kinky, and high style glamour.

voyage.name: M-BIA
voyage.content: Techno club below the arches of the S-Bahn with an industrial interior, changing decorations and techno and psytrance nights.

voyage.name: OHM
voyage.content: Techno club in the former battery room of the disused power plant which also hosts the Tresor and Kraftwerk venues. Has a very industrial ambience, ceramic tiles on the wall, a small dance floor, and a good sound system.

voyage.name: Tresor
voyage.content: The history of this club dates back to 1990s and the start of techno/house scene in Berlin. The old venue in the vault space of the former Wertheim department store in Leipziger Strasse was closed in 2005, but Tresor reopened in May 2007 in a decommissioned power plant in the southeast of Berlin-Mitte.

voyage.name: Clärchens Ballhaus
voyage.price: Entrance fee depending on event: usually free on weeknights, €5 on weekends
voyage.hours: Daily from 11:00 usually to 00:00 on weeknights, and around 04:00 on weekends); hot food 12:00-22:30, garden closes 23:00, dance starts 21:00
voyage.content: Traditional dance hall and restaurant established 1913. One of the few surviving Berlin ballrooms from the pre-WW1 era, featuring a hall of mirrors. Primarily known for its dance events (be it Disco, Swing, Salsa, Tango, Cha-Cha or "Schwoof", i.e. freestyle), it also hosts concerts, but you may as well just come for dinner or a drink. The venue has been a set for films like Inglourious Basterds and Stauffenberg.

voyage.name: Hotel Adlon
voyage.content: Unter den Linden 77 (Pariser Platz, Unter den Linden), Located directly at the Brandenburg Gate and was rated the best hotel of Europe in 2006.

voyage.name: Hotel de Rome
voyage.content: A very good bar and Italian restaurant.

voyage.name: Melia Berlin
voyage.content: Modern Spanish four star hotel, includes safe in room but no coffee making facilities and poor TV and air-conditioning . Good tapas bars and nice river views from breakfast. Good cold and hot breakfast options.

voyage.name: The Regent Berlin
voyage.content: Charlottenstraße 49. Former Four Seasons hotel now managed by the Taiwan-based Regent chain. Located next to Gendarmenmarkt near Unter Den Linden.

voyage.name: The Westin Grand Berlin
voyage.content: Five-star hotel provides newly decorated accommodations facing the famous boulevard. Pomp architecture of the GDR.

voyage.name: Hotel Augustinenhof
voyage.content: Awarded with the 'barrier free' signet, this is a comfort plus not only for people with disabilities but also for seniors, families with prams and travellers with lots of luggage.

voyage.name: Courtyard by Marriott Berlin City Centre
voyage.content: Axel Springer Straße 55, a two-minute walk to the subway and situated close to highlights.

voyage.name: Hilton Berlin
voyage.content: Mohrenstraße 30.

voyage.name: Mercure Hotel & Residenz Berlin Checkpoint Charlie
NH Berlin Mitte
voyage.content: Renovated in 2008, this hotel offers 392 spacious bedrooms, meeting rooms and a spa.

voyage.name: one80º Hostel Berlin
voyage.content: 6 minutes away from Alexanderplatz.

voyage.name: Park Inn by Radisson Hotel Berlin Alexanderplatz
voyage.content: Germany's tallest hotel at Alexanderplatz features unique views of Berlin.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Hotel, Berlin
voyage.content: The main attraction of the hotel was the AquaDom, the world's largest cylindrical aquarium containing one million litres of saltwater, until it exploded in December 2022.

voyage.name: Grand Hyatt Berlin
voyage.content: During the Berlinale film festival, this is the primary hotel to stay because most major attractions are within walking distance.

voyage.name: The Mandala Hotel
voyage.content: Hotel on Potsdamer Platz, Kulturforum, Neue Nationalgalerie and the Philharmony.

voyage.name: The Ritz-Carlton, Berlin
voyage.content: An unforgettable 5-star hotel.

voyage.name: Novotel Berlin Mitte
voyage.content: The only hotel on Museumsinsel

voyage.name: Art'otel Mitte
voyage.content: A stylish hotel though with smallish rooms. Good breakfast, double-check that your reservation includes it. Helpful staff.

voyage.name: Ballhaus Berlin Hostel
voyage.content: Berlin’s oldest hostel is housed in a unique old brick building which also hosts Berlin’s oldest ballroom, and now also one of Berlin’s oldest pubs, the infamous Alt-Berlin. Carrying on the tradition of the ballroom downstairs, the hostel's themes range from the previous golden 20s to the upcoming 20s.

voyage.name: The Circus Hostel
voyage.content: 2-bed rooms start at €28 per person, sleeping hall starts at €19. Not to be confused with the hotel of the same name across the street.

voyage.name: EasyHotel
voyage.content: Very basic, cheap and clean: small room with tiny bath room. The nearest metro station is on Rosenthaler Platz.

voyage.name: Gästehaus Berlin Mitte
voyage.price: Single room starts at €39, double room at €49 per room, dormitory at €19 per person

voyage.name: Heart of Gold Hostel Berlin
voyage.price: Private rooms start at €20/person, big dorms start at €9

voyage.name: Helter Skelter Hostel Berlin
voyage.content: Double rooms start at €46/room, big dorms start at €13.

voyage.name: St Christopher's Berlin
voyage.content: A new well maintained hostel with large public bar downstairs located in Mitte. Generally good security and friendly international staff. Part of a large independent hostel chain.

voyage.name: wombats City Hostel Berlin
voyage.content: All rooms with shower and toilet; free WLAN, bar with happy hour etc.

voyage.name: Amano Auguststraße
voyage.content: This stylish hotel of the Amano chain is recommended for travellers who like extremely minimalist design. It has a nice rooftop bar and a fashionable cocktail bar with DJs.

voyage.name: Circus Hotel
voyage.content: Rosenthalerstr. 1 - This stylish hotel is close to the Rosenthaler Platz U-Bahn, and is the more luxurious version of the Circus Hostel. Each room has an individual and colorful design. Breakfast included, free wifi, free laptops, DVDs, and iPods available to borrow. Reserve early and ask for an interior room if street noise bothers you at night, but some of the rooms on the street side have a magnificent view over R

voyage.name: ibis Styles Berlin Mitte
voyage.content: One of the four ibis Styles hotels in Berlin - make sure to put down the right address to avoid confusion. WiFi and breakfast included in all room prices as in all ibis Styles hotel.

voyage.name: Jugendgästehaus Berlin International
voyage.price: Four-bed rooms start at €23.50 (depending on age), ten-person-dormitories start at €15, all overnights including breakfast and bedsheets. HI-Hostel-membership required, international guests may also pay €3.10 extra for an overnight membership
voyage.content: Central location near Potsdam Square with quiet surroundings.

voyage.name: Hotel Berlin Berlin
voyage.content: A huge hotel occupying an entire block at the Lützowplatz, with many conference rooms and discounts for large parties and conventions.

voyage.name: Pestana Berlin Tiergarten Hotel
voyage.content: Located next to the Tiergarten park and zoo, in a quiet corner between embassies.

voyage.name: Pullman Berlin Schweitzerhof
voyage.content: The former Sofitel found a new lease of life as an ultra-modern Pullman. It is located in Budapester Straße, a relatively quiet upscale street running along the Zoologischer Garten. some distance away from U-Bahn or S-Bahn stations.
